To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photoconductivities of films formed from substituted PBIs vary significantly with substitution, and that this is due primarily to the different ways that the molecules pack, with the electronic properties of individual molecules being relatively insensitive to substituents.
the photoconductivities of PBI films vary with the substituent at the imide position and that this can be explained by the different packing of the molecules in the aggregates.
the photoconducting properties of self‐organized PBI aggregates depend strongly on the nature of the substituent at the imide position, which is in turn determined by the self‐assembly process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of organic materials for optoelectronic applications.
the synthesis of new materials and the development of novel synthetic methods.
developing new materials for organic electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self‐assembly and packing of the PBI is affected by the substitution pattern and that this in turn affects the photoconductivity.
the photoconductivities of self‐assemblies of substituted PBIs can vary strongly with the substituents and the packing of the self‐assembly.
the photoconducting properties of PBI films are strongly dependent on the nature of the substituent and the supramolecular assembly formed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the photoconducting properties of self‐organised PBIs can be tuned through the use of different substituents, and that the different packing motifs that result can be used to explain the different properties observed.
the photoconducting properties of self‐assembly PBI films can be controlled by supramolecular assembly.
we show how supramolecular self‐assembly can be used to control photoconductive properties in a PBI library, which is important for applications in organic electronics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electronic structure of a self‐assembled PBI aggregate is strongly dependent on the packing of the molecules in the aggregate, with the packing in turn dependent on the choice of substituent.

it is possible to tune the properties of self‐assembly by changing the substituents, even when the electronic properties of these substituents do not change significantly, and that the resulting changes can be used to tune the optoelectronics of the resulting films.

the optoelectroinc properties of PBI aggregates depend strongly on their structure, and that it is possible to optimise the properties by controlling this structure through the choice of substitution pattern.
